name: Arrays & Hashing
body: Use a set for membership; a dict or Counter for frequencies or value-to-index lookup. Repeated scans often signal a reusable summary. Avoid hashing when ordering or worst-case guarantees matter. Hash operations are expected O(1); total space is usually O(n). Check duplicates, empty inputs, and whether to look up before inserting.

name: Two Pointers
description: Maintain an invariant while moving two boundaries.
body: Consider two pointers for sorted pairs, partitioning, or opposite-end constraints. State what is already settled outside the pointers. Move a pointer only when its discarded candidates cannot improve the answer. Sorting may change indices and cost O(n log n). Do not use opposite-end elimination without a monotonic argument. Each pointer moving at most n times yields O(n) work.

name: Sliding Window
body: Fixed windows remove one item and add one; variable windows expand and shrink while maintaining a measurable condition. A frequency dict tracks multiplicity; a set only tracks membership. Use when valid boundaries move monotonically. Arbitrary negative-sum constraints may break that property. Track whether counts mean missing items or distinct requirements. Two moving boundaries give O(n) work when updates are constant time.
template:
left = 0
for right, value in enumerate(values):
    add(value)
    while invalid():
        remove(values[left])
        left += 1
    record_window(left, right)

name: Stacks & Monotonic Stacks
description: Keep unresolved work in last-in, first-out order.
body: Use a stack for nesting, parsing, undo, and unresolved nearest-boundary questions. A monotonic stack removes entries once they can be finalized. Push/pop once gives amortized O(n), even inside a nested loop. A queue instead serves earliest work first. Be precise about equal values, empty pops, operator order, and sentinels.

name: Binary Search
description: Discard half of an ordered search space.
body: Use sorted values or a monotone predicate. Prefer a half-open [lo, hi) boundary template; the unresolved indices are [lo, hi), while the first feasible boundary remains between lo and hi inclusive. When lo equals hi, that boundary is determined. Binary search needs random access and monotonicity, not simply a numeric answer. Each iteration halves the range: O(log n) comparisons, O(1) auxiliary space. Test empty ranges and first/last candidates.

name: Linked Lists
description: Reason about node identity and pointer ownership.
body: Use pointer rewiring when random access is unavailable. A dummy node simplifies changes at the head; slow/fast pointers compare traversal speeds. Save a successor before overwriting next. Do not confuse equal values with identical nodes. Traversal costs O(n); index access is also O(n). Watch cycles, one-node lists, shared nodes, and detached chains.
template:
dummy = Node()
tail = dummy
while node is not None:
    successor = node.next
    tail.next = node
    tail = node
    node = successor

name: Trees & Binary Search Trees
description: Combine subtree answers or visit one level at a time.
body: DFS uses O(h) stack space and naturally combines children; BFS uses O(width) space and exposes levels. A BST ordering rule applies to entire subtrees, not only immediate children. Define what recursion returns and the empty-subtree answer. Prefer iteration for very deep trees in Python. A full traversal costs O(n). Height can be n in a skewed tree.

name: Graphs & Grid Traversal
description: Explore connections, dependencies, and shortest unweighted paths.
body: DFS explores a branch; BFS finds minimum edge count in unweighted graphs. Mark discovered vertices when enqueuing to avoid repeated work. Track all components; directed cycle detection needs active-path state or indegrees. A grid is an implicit graph. Traversals cost O(V+E), or O(rows*cols) for bounded neighbors. Weighted paths need a different algorithm. Check disconnected nodes and mutation permissions.

name: Heaps & Priority Queues
description: Access the next extreme without fully sorting.
body: Use a heap for incremental selection, top-k maintenance, or merging sorted streams. Python heapq is a min-heap; negate numeric priorities for a max-heap. Push/pop costs O(log k) for heap size k, heapify O(k). A heap is not globally sorted and arbitrary deletion is costly. Include a tie-breaker when payloads cannot be compared.
template:
import heapq
heap = []
for priority, serial, item in items:
    heapq.heappush(heap, (priority, serial, item))
priority, serial, item = heapq.heappop(heap)

name: Intervals
description: Turn overlap questions into ordered boundary decisions.
body: Sort intervals by the boundary required by your proof. Merging uses start order; selecting nonoverlapping work often uses end order. Define whether touching endpoints overlap. Sorting costs O(n log n), then a scan may be linear. Greedy selection fails when arbitrary weights require comparing future profit. Check empty lists and contained intervals.
prerequisites: Sorting; binary search for weighted cases

name: Backtracking & Recursion
description: Enumerate choices with reversible local state.
body: Describe state, legal choices, stopping condition, and how to undo a choice. Use when all combinations or paths are requested; exponential work may be inherent. Prune impossible branches without discarding valid solutions. Copy a path when storing it. Distinguish reuse from one-time choices and distinguish path-local from global visited state. Output storage often dominates complexity.

name: Dynamic Programming
description: Cache the answers to overlapping subproblems.
body: Define a state in one sentence, then list choices and base cases. A transition must depend on smaller or already-computed states. Memoization explores reachable states; tabulation gives control over order and memory. Complexity is number of states times work per state, plus output. Avoid DP when no subproblems repeat. Test unreachable states and empty prefixes; loop direction controls reuse.

name: Tries
description: Share prefixes across many string lookups.
body: A trie stores one edge per symbol; terminal markers distinguish complete words from prefixes. Insert/search cost O(L) for word length L. It is useful for prefix queries, while a hash set is often simpler for full-word membership. Memory can be large with per-node dictionaries. Test a word that is also another word's prefix.
template:
node = root
for char in word:
    node = node.children.setdefault(char, TrieNode())
node.terminal = True

name: Strings & Simulation
description: Translate a precise specification into a small state machine.
body: Track the minimal state required to process the next character or boundary. Separate whitespace, sign, digits, carry, and stopping rules when relevant. Python strings are immutable: repeated prepending can become quadratic; collect characters and join once. Matrix simulation needs explicit boundary invariants. Check empty input, overflow rules, and final carry.
template:
output = []
state = initial_state
for token in tokens:
    state, emitted = step(state, token)
    output.extend(emitted)
answer = "".join(output)

name: Greedy & Counting Invariants
description: Prove why a local choice preserves a global answer.
body: A greedy step needs an exchange or cancellation argument. Counting often identifies a bottleneck or an unavoidable lower bound. Do not use greedy just because a local choice looks good; weighted constraints may require DP. Describe what remains possible after each choice. Confirm assumptions such as an existing majority or a fixed alphabet.
template:
state = initial_summary
for value in values:
    state = update_invariant(state, value)
# Verify any candidate if the problem does not guarantee existence.
